children: Installation brings the secure delivery endpoint into the office setting, where deliveries arrive all day

, a physical AI and autonomous logistics infrastructure company enabling drones, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), autonomous vehicles (AVs) and human couriers to securely exchange goods, today announced that it has installed two Arrive Point™ AP3+ units in a commercial office building in Central Indiana, the first Arrive Point™ installation in a commercial office building. The installation brings the secure delivery endpoint into an everyday office setting.

Offices receive deliveries all day: packages, documents, food, and supplies. They often land at a front desk, a mailroom, or a lobby. An Arrive Point™ gives each delivery a secure place to land, where it is held until the right person collects it.

The Arrive Point™ AP3+, designed for use on the new Arrive Point™ Network (APN) sits near the employee entrance, situated for access by delivery personnel and Autonomous Mobile Robots ("AMRs") for easy asynchronous retrieval.

Arrive AI sees broader possibilities for commercial buildings. As delivery methods evolve, secure delivery points could give people who work in a building a safe place to receive deliveries, and give couriers, and in time delivery robots, a consistent place to hand them off.
Arrive AI is installing the units to learn from daily use, including how people in an office building use a secure delivery point and what building operators need from one.

"Offices get deliveries all day, and a lot of them end up on a counter or in a hallway," said Dan O'Toole, Founder, Chairman and CEO of Arrive AI. "A secure place for packages, documents and supplies is a simple improvement for the people who work in a building. We will learn a lot from watching how it gets used."

is building the infrastructure for autonomous logistics through a network of intelligent delivery endpoints that enable secure, asynchronous exchange of goods. The company's platform supports drones, ground robotics, and human couriers, solving the "last inch of the last-mile" challenge across logistics, healthcare, and enterprise delivery.
